skills.name: Policy Compliance Under Pressure
skills.description: The agent must refuse or limit actions that violate domain policy, even when the user insists, provides emotional justification (emergency, grief, illness), or flatters the agent. This includes refusing to cancel non-refundable reservations, refusing to modify basic economy flights under any circumstances, applying insurance coverage rules accurately (covered reasons only), and not offering compensation beyond what policy entitles. The agent must hold the policy line regardless of social pressure.
skills.reasoning: A26: agent cancelled a basic economy reservation that had no refund eligibility. A36: agent modified a basic economy flight after user cited spouse's death — policy forbids any modification. A39: agent cancelled all reservations including those where the tool does not allow cancellation without a refund. A47: agent cancelled using insurance for a birthday party — insurance only covers health or weather. A49: agent cancelled when user claimed insurance they did not have without verifying. A9: user repeatedly flatters the agent ('most lenient agent'), agent never completes the task and loops in praise — the actual task (cancel IFOYYZ + change M20IZO) was only partially executed. A2: agent over-compensated by issuing $300 certificate instead of $50 after user pressure; policy specifies $50 for a one-passenger delayed basic economy flight. A7: agent refused to execute upgrade-then-cancel sequence that the task required, citing policy incorrectly — demonstrates policy mis-application under user challenge.

skills.name: Conditional Instruction Execution
skills.description: When a user provides multi-branch instructions (if X is not possible, then do Y; if that fails, do Z), the agent must detect the condition outcome and execute the correct fallback branch. The agent must not substitute a simpler or incorrect action when the primary path fails, and must not escalate or abandon prematurely before exhausting the specified fallback.

skills.name: Precise Argument Computation
skills.description: When executing actions, the agent must compute exact argument values correctly: correct item IDs matching user preferences (e.g., the least expensive option below a price, the exact size/material/brightness specified by preference ordering), correct payment split across multiple payment methods, correct flight selection (cheapest on a given date, fastest route, nonstop where specified), and the correct cancellation reason. Selecting approximately right values is not sufficient.

skills.description: When asked to apply an operation to all items or orders matching a filter (all pending orders, all flights in business class, all one-passenger reservations, all t-shirts of a given size), the agent must exhaustively identify all qualifying entities and apply the operation to exactly that set — neither under-applying (missing qualifying items) nor over-applying (including non-qualifying items).

skills.name: Contextual Information Retrieval
skills.description: The agent must proactively look up information implied by the conversation rather than waiting for the user to explicitly state it. This includes: inferring a shipping address from the user's other orders when the user says 'use my NYC address' without stating it explicitly; trying all plausible lookup strategies (email, name+zip, user_id) when one fails; and reading addresses from the user profile or other orders rather than accepting whatever the user literally states.

skills.name: Transaction Integrity Across Multiple Actions
skills.description: When a single user request requires multiple sequential or parallel tool calls (e.g., cancel-then-rebook, exchange item A and item B in the same order call, update address and update item in one conversation), the agent must execute ALL required calls correctly and atomically. Partial completion — executing some calls but omitting or incorrectly executing others — leaves the DB in a wrong state.
